sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 13: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet' — a blanket remark about the survey's broad phonetic transcription, not about Kein, which is not among the languages covered (Kein/Bemal was first recorded in Z'graggen's 1971-72 fieldwork).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid kein1239 and reference tables for kein1239, koko1271 (Kokon) and mabu1247 (Mabuso)
sources.note: Only two references for Kein (Z'graggen 1975, 1980), none descriptive. Kokon-subgroup references (64) are all Girawa (Lillie, Gassmann; Gasaway & Sims 1992 'Girawa grammar') or Munit ('Berin phonology', Elliott & Elliott 1977); Mabuso references (148) add Amele, Bau, Nobonob, Wagi items — no Kein-specific description anywhere.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. xvi+199 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kein appears as 'Bemal' (column C4) in a ~300-item comparative wordlist. Introduction section 6 (pp. viii-ix) says the transcription is 'semi-phonemic' and lists fluctuating consonants per language (Bemal: s~j, z~dz~zy, l~r, d~r); vowel length is written (e.g. 'man' du:) but stress is never marked and the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the volume (checked in both the ANU text layer and a fresh extracted text run). No statement on Kein stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification overview; Bemal (C4) appears only in comparative pronoun/lexical tables. No phonology section, no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Typological survey of the Western Madang District with brief phonological statements for the 'Madang Phylum' as a whole (absence of certain phonemes); Kein/Bemal was not yet surveyed (no occurrence of the name in the text layer) and the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur. Nothing on Kein stress.
